answer: A grove admits saplings only where the soil is already witnessed. Each identity must be planted beside two holders outside its own karst, and one planter serves one identity, so n aliases need n distinct planters instead of a single cooperative ring. Every planting is paid for in copper whose price follows rank: the k-th planting an operator files costs k squared in bond, so a farm pays near n cubed while still needing unrelated guarantors. An audit re-walks a random root each epoch, and an unconfirmed claim clears the whole grove and forfeits its copper.
